ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is x(cm), and the horizontal axis is t(s). The curve is a sinusoidal x-t graph of simple harmonic motion: at t=0 it passes through x=0 and the slope is positive; at about t=2 s it reaches x=+1 cm; at t=4 s it crosses zero again and is downward; at about t=6 s it reaches x=-1 cm; at t=8 s it again passes through x=0 in the same upward zero-crossing direction. Therefore the amplitude A=1 cm and the period T=8 s. Reasoning: according to the graph, the displacement can be written as x(t)=A sin(2πt/T)=sin(πt/4) cm. Acceleration is the second derivative of displacement with respect to time: a(t)=d²x/dt²=-(π/4)^2 sin(πt/4). Substituting t=4/3 s gives sin(π/3)=√3/2, so a=-(π²/16)(√3/2)=-√3π²/32 cm/s².

raw_record.question_text: The x-t graph of a particle undergoing simple harmonic motion is shown below. What is the acceleration of the particle at t = 4/3 s?

method.method_draft: Read the x-t graph as a sine curve: the particle passes through x=0 at t=0 with positive slope, reaches +1 cm at about t=2 s, crosses zero at t=4 s, reaches -1 cm at about t=6 s, and repeats the same zero-crossing direction at t=8 s. Thus A=1 cm and T=8 s, so write x(t)=A sin(2πt/T)=sin(πt/4) cm. Differentiate twice to get a(t)=d²x/dt²=-(π/4)^2 sin(πt/4). Substitute t=4/3 s, so sin(π/3)=√3/2, giving a=-(π²/16)(√3/2)=-√3π²/32 cm/s².

method.method_draft: From the graph, identify A=1 cm and T=8 s. Since the graph crosses x=0 upward at t=0, after t=4/3 s the phase advanced is θ=2π(t/T)=2π(4/3)/8=π/3. Therefore the displacement at that instant is x=A sin θ=1·sin(π/3)=√3/2 cm. Use the SHM acceleration-displacement relation directly: a=-ω²x, with ω=2π/T=π/4 s⁻¹. Hence a=-(π/4)²(√3/2)=-√3π²/32 cm/s².
